properties.name: Anthony rules on null unsets: a null on additive history or a status is refused, and a client sending null for every empty field clears them
properties.rationale: Anthony, 2026-10-25: "Go with your recommendation on null unsets". A judgement recorded as history (distinct_from is ADDITIVE in the schema) must not be erasable by a null, and a status reset to its default by a null would read a realized capability as planned with no owner's word; both now refuse by name, and a status refusal points at the tool that moves a status deliberately. Keeping null-clears for clients that send null for every empty field is his choice, made visible in the changelog. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: PR #797, after Anthony's ruling: nulls.rs refuse_history_and_status refuses a null on a property whose schema description says ADDITIVE (distinct_from) and on `status` (naming set_requirement/capability/decision/verification/epoch_status where one serves the type, else asking for the status meant), before anything is kept; the guard test asks both of every constructor (failing first on head 4fb009113: 31 problems across 13 constructors). The changelog fragment states the null-for-every-empty-field behaviour change for MCP clients.
